question: blog-seasonal-cleanout-guide.html answers only 3 FAQ question(s) versus a 6-question average among its comparable siblings — is there enough evidence that this page specific topic has specific, genuinely useful practical questions not yet answered there, that would justify adding to its FAQ?
source: Web search for "seasonal junk removal cleanout FAQ questions homeowners ask spring fall" — aggregate of industry/competitor FAQ and blog pages (Flannery Handymen, Lansing Junk Removal, Mr Junk, EZ CleanUp, and others)
evidence: Multiple independent junk-removal industry FAQ/blog pages recurrently answer "how far in advance should I book during a busy season" as a distinct question from "does cost change by season" — Mile High's existing FAQ only has the latter, not the former.
Several of the same sources separately call out fall yard-waste logistics (bagged leaves/branches) as its own common question, distinct from the general seasonal-cost question.

This is a pattern observed across generic industry content, not a measurement of search volume or ranking position for Mile High's own page — observing that a topic appears often does NOT establish local search demand (SERP presence vs. search volume).
limitations: This is a generic cross-industry content pattern, not Denver/Mile-High-specific evidence, and carries no search-volume or Search Console data at all. On its own this is too weak to justify a change — see the companion official-government research result for the specific, locally-grounded evidence that actually tips this finding.
recommendation: Insufficient on its own. See the companion result citing Denver's official LeafDrop program for a concrete, locally-specific angle worth considering.
